Subject: Please reopen: PR #812 changed the default wavelength frame

I did read the changelog. I have now traced the offset to a default changed in PR #812, rather than a problem with my wavelength calibration.

In LineList.__init__, the default changed from wave_frame='air' to wave_frame='vacuum'. My optical slit spectra are wavelength-calibrated in air, so with the same inputs and config, 2.5.0 now uses rest wavelengths in a different frame. Near H-alpha, the vacuum/air wavelength ratio is approximately 1.00028. That matches the direction and approximate size of the redshift offset I reported, corresponding to about 83 km/s. Downgrading restores the previous results; explicitly setting the frame also fixes it.

For anyone finding this thread with the same issue, the workaround for air-calibrated spectra is:

LineList(..., wave_frame='air')

Use the frame appropriate to your data; this is not a recommendation to set every dataset to air.

I am frustrated that this was dismissed as “almost certainly” my calibration or config and marked solved without establishing the cause. I spent two days investigating my calibration and re-reducing arc lamps for 40 spectra unnecessarily. Telling me to “do basic checks” was not warranted by the evidence in the thread.

“Works fine for me” does not test this specific case without specifying the wavelength frame and configuration. Data already in vacuum, or radio data, would not necessarily expose this optical air/vacuum mismatch. I do not know what your test used. m_okonkwo also reported a possible offset here, which was another reason to investigate rather than close the thread.

The CHANGES entry says only “Refactor LineList and spectral frame handling (#812).” That does not tell users that a scientifically consequential default has changed, and there was no deprecation warning.

Please reopen this thread. Could the maintainers add an explicit CHANGES entry describing the default change and migration workaround, and consider a warning when wave_frame is not explicitly set? This needs to be discoverable without users having to inspect a PR diff.
